subject: Token emit backlog affecting streaming responses - immediate mitigations and next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Zhang <amy@quercusretail.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Token emit backlog affecting streaming responses - immediate mitigations and next steps

Hi Amy —

Thanks for the flag this morning. We’re seeing an elevated token-emission backlog on the regional streaming shard serving your production region, which is increasing end-to-end response latency for streaming chat sessions (clients observing delayed chunk arrival and occasional short pauses).

Immediate status: engineering has identified a surge in request concurrency combined with a suboptimal KV-cache eviction pattern on the shard pool (RWI-7842). We have a mitigation in progress that will reduce backlog within ~45-90 minutes, and we’re executing temporary routing to less-saturated capacity to stabilize sessions.

Short-term mitigations I recommend on your side (safe to apply without model changes):
- Reduce client-side "max_buffered_tokens" to 32 (from 128) to avoid large prefetched frames.
- If you can tolerate non-streaming responses during the next 60–90 minutes, switch the endpoint to the non-streaming /v1/generate path as a fallback.
- Increase client-side receive timeout to 35s to avoid premature disconnects during bursts.

We’ll keep you updated every 30 minutes or when the backlog drops. I’ll follow up with a brief post-incident summary and permanent remediation plan.

Apologies for the disruption — we know low-latency streaming is critical for Quercus’s checkout assistant.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks | Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Token emit backlog affecting streaming responses - immediate mitigations and next steps

Thanks Dylan — we’re seeing visible pauses in our live chat flow. A couple notes from our side:
- Impact: agents report 1–3 second gaps between partial responses; in some cases the UI shows a stall for up to ~7s.
- Scope: appears to affect about 18% of active sessions in US-WEST region.
- Workarounds: switching to non-streaming causes a spike in perceived latency for long replies, so we’d prefer to remain streaming if possible.

We’ll try the "max_buffered_tokens" change now and report back. Any ETA on when routing to other capacity will complete?

— Amy
Head of Product Operations, Quercus Retail

Date: 2028-07-18T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Token emit backlog affecting streaming responses - escalation and asks

Team — forwarding the customer note. TL;DR: surge + KV cache churn causing token emission backlog on us-west streaming shard group. Customer prefers to remain streaming if we can stabilize.

Requests / immediate action items:
1) Marissa: can you coordinate a capacity bump on the us-west streaming pool and activate the emergency routing policy (route_avoid_degraded) for Quercus workload? Estimate impact window and when RPS will return to normal.
2) Laura: need a short rollback-safe config to adjust cache TTL heuristics that reduces eviction churn (patch should be < 30 lines in runtime config). Can you triage & prepare patch?
3) Sean: please pull shard-level traces for the last 90 minutes and include top-5 keys by eviction rate. We’ll attach telemetry to the incident doc.

I’ll keep Amy updated and provide client-side guidance to reduce failure modes in the interim.

— Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Amy Zhang <amy@quercusretail.com>, ops@quercusretail.com
Date: 2028-07-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token emit backlog affecting streaming responses - escalation and asks

Update for Quercus + internal owners:

What we did (11:00 PDT):
- Routed 40% of Quercus streaming traffic to an underutilized host group in us-west and increased concurrency slots for the remaining pool by 20%.
- Applied a temporary KY-ttl bump to reduce cache evictions (runtime flag: kv_cache_ttl_ms=45000 -> 90000).

Observed effect (11:45 PDT):
- Token emission backlog reduced by ~62% on the affected shards.
- Customer telemetry shows a drop in multi-second stalls; median inter-chunk gap improved from ~1.8s to ~0.4s.

Recommended customer-side changes (safe to revert later):
- Keep max_buffered_tokens at 32 for the next 2 hours.
- If you have a batching layer, temporarily limit parallel user-connections-per-worker to 10 to smooth request bursts.

Attachments: temporary-config-suggestions.pdf (contains exact runtime flags and our rollback steps).

We’ll run the next observation sweep at 12:30 PDT and confirm clearance. If metrics remain stable for 90 minutes we’ll start reverting temporary routing.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Incident Response Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-07-18T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Resolution & next steps — token emit backlog (RWI-7842)

Hi Amy — quick update and next steps now that the acute backlog is cleared.

Current state: backlog metrics for Quercus traffic in US-WEST are within normal bounds (95th pct inter-chunk gap < 1s) and we’ve started a cautious rollback of the temporary routing.

Immediate customer takeaways:
- We recommend leaving your client max_buffered_tokens at 32 until tomorrow morning PDT to let cache hit-rates converge.
- Optional: enable jittered client reconnects (randomized 200–500ms) if you observe transient bursts while we revert routing.

What we’re doing next:
1) Post-incident summary: we’ll share a one-page timeline and a short postmortem by EOD tomorrow that covers root cause (concurrency surge + KV eviction churn), permanent mitigations (auto-scale tweaks + cache heuristic changes), and the rollout plan.
2) Follow-up: Laura will propose a permanent KV-cache tuning and an automatic shard-eviction detector in the next 5 working days.
3) Credits: We’ll propose a service credit for the impacted window — I’ll include options in the postmortem.

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the timeline and the permanent changes. Please suggest a time window that works for your team.

Thanks again for your patience — we understand the surface area this touches for checkout experience.

— Dylan
